question: What is the main reason for making a special bed in the hospital?

options.A: To make the hospital ward look tidy for morning inspection
options.B: To give student nurses practice in basic domestic chores
options.C: To meet specific therapeutic or diagnostic needs of a patient
options.D: To reduce the total amount of hospital laundry generated daily

explanation: Spot on! Special beds are arranged to support patients with specific medical conditions, way beyond just normal daily tidying.

question: Why must bed sheets in a hospital stay completely free of wrinkles?

options.A: Wrinkles make it difficult for the patient to adjust their pillows
options.B: Wrinkles signal to visitors that the nursing staff is careless
options.C: Wrinkles trap trapped air and cause the room temperature to rise
options.D: Wrinkles increase friction and pressure on the skin, leading to sores

explanation: You got it! Smooth sheets protect your patient's skin by preventing friction and pressure points that cause painful bedsores.

question: As a student nurse, why should you avoid shaking dirty bed linen in the air?

options.A: Shaking disperses dust and microorganisms into the surrounding room
options.B: Shaking makes the linen difficult to fold into the laundry bag
options.C: Shaking creates loud noises that startle resting patients
options.D: Shaking causes the fabric to stretch out of shape quickly

explanation: Correct! Shaking soiled sheets sends germs and dust flying into the air, which can easily spread infection around the ward.

question: What is the proper way to hold clean linen when you are about to make a bed?

options.A: Tuck the clean linen under your arm to keep both hands free
options.B: Rest the clean linen pile on the patient's bedside table for easy access
options.C: Place the clean linen on the floor temporarily while gathering equipment
options.D: Hold the clean linen away from your uniform to prevent contamination

explanation: Well done! Your uniform picks up germs from different places, so keeping clean sheets away from your body keeps them germ-free for the patient.

question: What is another popular name for an admission bed in the ward?
explanation: That's right! We call it an open bed because the top covers are folded back nicely to welcome the new patient.

question: How do you usually arrange the top covers on an admission bed?

options.A: Tucked tightly all around to keep the mattress completely warm
options.B: Folded or fan-folded to the side to allow easy patient transfer
options.C: Arranged in a tight roll directly down the middle of the mattress
options.D: Removed entirely and stored in the ward linen cupboard

explanation: Correct! Folding the top covers to the side means an incoming patient can slip straight into bed without struggling with heavy blankets.

question: Why do we place a waterproof sheet on an operation (surgical) bed?

options.A: To protect the mattress from bodily fluids, blood, and drainage
options.B: To anchor the top blankets securely to the bed frame
options.C: To keep the patient cool during high fever episodes
options.D: To provide extra cushioning for bony prominences

explanation: Spot on! Patients coming from theatre might bleed or vomit, so a waterproof sheet keeps the mattress safe and clean.

question: You are preparing a recovery bed for a patient coming back from theatre. Which item must you keep ready at the bedside?

options.C: Bedside dining tray and reading lamp
options.D: A heavy woolen floor rug and extra pillows

explanation: Great job! Patients waking up from anesthesia can easily choke on saliva or vomit, so having a suction machine and a basin nearby is a lifesaver.

question: Which breathing problem makes a cardiac bed necessary for a patient?
explanation: Exactly! Orthopnea is when a patient struggles to breathe while lying flat, which is why cardiac patients need an upright bed setup.

question: Why do we place a footrest or pillow at the bottom of a cardiac bed?

options.A: To prevent the patient from sliding downward while in a sitting position
options.B: To provide a stable surface for the patient to attach leg exercise bands
options.C: To improve blood circulation directly to the lower extremities
options.D: To stop the mattress from sagging in the middle of the frame

explanation: You nailed it! Because the bed is propped up high, gravity tries to pull the patient down. The footrest keeps them comfortably in place.

question: What is the very first thing you should do before making any hospital bed?

options.A: Strip all the old linens off the mattress simultaneously
options.B: Lock the bed wheels and adjust it to a comfortable working height
options.C: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the ward
options.D: Remove all pillows and place them on a nearby chair

explanation: Correct! Safety first: lock the wheels so the bed doesn't roll away, and raise it so you don't hurt your back while working.

question: Which action shows that you are using good body mechanics while making a bed?

options.A: Keeping the hospital bed in its lowest position throughout the procedure
options.B: Stretching your arms far across the mattress without moving your feet
options.C: Using leg muscles with a wide base of support when moving heavy items
options.D: Twisting rapidly at the waist to transfer linen from one hand to the other

explanation: Wonderful! Using your legs and keeping a wide stance protects your back from injury during nursing duties.
